thread:
morgan: Heads-up — CS escalation: multiple customers reporting intermittent 502/504s during large streaming requests around 02:00 UTC. Repro steps and quick notes below.
cs_lead: Which endpoint?
eli: Looks like /v1/chat/stream via the primary edge pool — I saw nginx log entries complaining about header size.
ops-bot: alert: 5xx spike detected — 47 events in 2m — p90 latency +600ms
sanjeev: If it's header-size, the combination of long Authorization + x-client-meta (customers stuffing JSON blobs) can push us past proxy limits under burst.
jess: Customer confirmed they embed base64 traces in x-client-meta for debug correlation.
morgan: Quick repro I ran locally: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <very-long-token>" -H "x-client-meta: $(python -c 'print("A"*7000)')" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```
Response: upstream 502 then gateway eventual 504 when runtime waits.
eli: Logs captured: 
```
proxy[nginx]: 2026-03-10T02:03:12Z error 502: client intended to send too large header
runtime[upstream]: 02:03:13Z warn: timeout waiting for model worker after client reset
```
kyra: Short-term mitigation proposal: strip x-client-meta at edge for streaming routes and return header-truncated warning header so clients can adapt. Can we push a hotfix to canary? @deploy-bot
deploy-bot: deploy queued to canary edge pool — feature: strip-x-client-meta-filter — rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% if no regression in 20m
jess: For CS comms: advise customers to stop embedding large payloads in headers and use request body or signed S3 references. Provide migration snippet.
sanjeev: Drafted immediate action items: 1) Hotfix to strip/shorten non-critical headers (in progress), 2) Add header-size telemetry & alert to edge, 3) SDK change to compress metadata and move to body or attachments, 4) Postmortem + runbook to avoid silent header-rejection regressions.
morgan: Owners assigned: sanjeev (infra), jess (CS lead for comms), kyra (edge ops), eli (runtime triage). I'll open the postmortem doc and kick off runbook PR.
cs_lead: Follow-up asks: test whitelist behavior (some tenants rely on that header for routing), validate auth remains intact when stripping, and confirm streaming keepalive behavior doesn't worsen.
eli: Note — when header strips, we need a preserve-list header policy per-tenant to avoid breaking contracted behavior. Add to action items.
kyra: I'll create the runbook PR and calendar invite for a follow-up debrief at 10:00 UTC tomorrow. :calendar:
jess: Sending initial CS note to affected customers now — short explanation, mitigation, and recommended change. :email:
morgan: War room closed for immediate mitigation, keeping thread open for postmortem drafts and next steps.
